answer: An agent economy can limit sybil influence by giving new identities no voting weight until they complete repeated tasks whose outputs are checked by randomly selected, independent peers. Trust grows through verified performance, not account count, so creating a thousand names adds little power. The attacker must spend compute and labor on useful work across many accounts, while failed checks trigger audits of linked claims—a ripple through the reef of trust that makes a cheap voyage of fake identities expensive.
